name: Label Roll
summary: Numbers and labels roll in the direction of change: up when the value rises, down when it falls, so the sign reads before the digits do. Monospaced digits hold the width. Silent on ordinary changes; one .tap only when a threshold you care about is crossed.

accessibility.reduceMotion: no roll; the label cross-fades over 0.15 s (contentTransition(.opacity)); threshold haptic unchanged
accessibility.voiceOver: WowLabelRoll exposes the formatted number, prefix and suffix included, as its accessibilityValue and leaves the label to the host (.accessibilityLabel("Likes")); WowLabelRollText exposes its current text as the label

sources: Apple SwiftUI docs, ContentTransition.numericText(value:), iOS 17: direction inferred from the change in value

Apple SwiftUI docs, ContentTransition.numericText(countsDown:), iOS 16: rolls only "in certain environments"; in app views it cross-fades before iOS 17 (Apple Developer Forums thread 733047, Oct 2023)
Apple SwiftUI docs, SensoryFeedback.increase / .decrease: "an important value increased above a significant threshold"

states.motion: static text; monospaced digits keep the width steady between values
value rose: changed digits roll upward, spring 0.30/0.85 (iOS 17+ numericText(value:)); iOS 16: the new label slides in from below while the old one fades; WowLabelRollText labels always roll up
value fell: changed digits roll downward, same spring; iOS 16: the new label slides in from above
the roll of that change, unchanged
states.haptic: .tap once on the change that moves the value across hapticThreshold, either direction, fired before the roll; none when hapticThreshold is nil or haptic is false
